title: Next Greater Element II
prompt: Given a circular integer array `nums` (the last element's next element is the first element of the array), return an array `result` where `result[i]` is the next greater number for `nums[i]`, considering the circular nature of the array. If it doesn't exist for `nums[i]`, `result[i] = -1`.

examples.explanation: The first 1's next greater is 2. The 2's next greater doesn't exist. The second 1's next greater, wrapping around, is the 2 at index 1.

hints: The circular wraparound means an element near the end might find its next greater element near the beginning — simulate that without physically duplicating the whole array if you want to save space.
Use the standard monotonic decreasing stack of indices for next-greater-element, but iterate 2n times using index i % n to simulate wrapping around once.
Only push each index once (during the first pass, i.e. when i < n) — the second lap is purely for resolving elements still on the stack, not for adding new candidates.

solution.approach: Simulate two laps around the array (indices 0..2n-1, using i % n to wrap) with a monotonic decreasing stack of indices awaiting their next greater element. Whenever the current value beats the value at the index on top of the stack, pop it and record the current value as its answer. Only push the index during the first lap (i < n); the second lap exists purely to let elements near the end discover a next-greater element that appears earlier in the array. Anything still on the stack after both laps has no next greater element (-1).
